question: The project to expand Florence airport, its impact on Natura 2000 sites and the potential implementation of the derogation provided for by the Habitats Directive (Directive 92/43/EEC)
The ‘masterplan’ for the expansion of Florence Amerigo Vespucci airport calls for the construction of a new runway that could have major repercussions for the surrounding areas.

On 12 November 2025, the Italian Environment and Culture Ministries issued a joint decree (DM-2025-0000678) in which they highlighted the inadequacy of the landscape report submitted as part of the masterplan’s landscape authorisation procedure.

In addition, the Technical Committee for Environmental Impact Verification pointed out in Opinion No 106 that the planned mitigation measures will not be enough to rule out residual adverse effects that could compromise the integrity of the nearby Natura 2000 sites.

The committee therefore issued a negative environmental implications assessment, which means that the project will only go ahead if it can obtain a derogation under Article 6(4) of the Habitats Directive (Directive 92/43/EEC). Local councils are complaining that previous mitigation and compensation measures were not implemented and have announced that they will oppose the masterplan in court.
In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the Florence airport masterplan and will it verify its compliance with the Habitats Directive?
Does the Commission believe that the conditions to obtain a derogation under Article 6(4) of the Habitats Directive have been met?
What criteria will the Commission use to assess the airport project’s compatibility with the EU’s environmental and landscape protection objectives?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.3.2026) While information on the Florence airport masterplan is publicly available on the website of the Italian Minister for the Environment and Energy Security1, to date the Commission has not received from the Italian authorities a notification under Article 6(4) of the Habitats Directive2.
For this reason, the Commission is not in a position to comment as to whether the conditions to obtain a derogation under Article 6(4) of the Habitats Directive have been met.

Such a notification is required in cases where plans or projects are found to have a significant negative effect on a Natura 2000 site, where there are no alternative solutions and where they must be carried out for imperative reasons of overriding public interest.

The Commission systematically examines any such notification to assess whether the requirements of Article 6(3) and (4) of the Habitats Directive were duly respected, including an assessment of the imperative reasons of overriding public interest that would justify the realisation of the plan or project in question.
The assessment is based on the requirements set out in the Directive as well as on the Commission guidelines on the provisions of Article 6(3) and (4) of the Habitats Directive3.
1 https://va.mite.gov.it/it-IT/Oggetti/Documentazione/9937/14638?RaggruppamentoID=1137. 2 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and

flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992. 3 Commission notice - Assessment of plans and projects in relation to Natura 2000 sites – Methodological guidance on the provisions of Article 6(3) and (4) of the Habitats Directive 92/43/EEC, OJ C 437, 28.10.2021.
